author: PhillyInquirer
title: Phillies' Zack Wheeler Frustrated After Early Hook Ends Five-Inning Streak
text:
Ace pitcher Zack Wheeler was visibly upset after being pulled in the fifth inning of the Phillies' 10-6 win over the Pirates, ending his streak of 53 straight starts with at least five innings pitched.
Zack Wheeler , the Philadelphia Phillies ' ace pitcher, expressed frustration after being removed from Wednesday night's game against the Pittsburgh Pirates before completing five innings. Wheeler pitched 4.2 innings, allowing four runs on nine hits with one walk and ten strikeouts, totaling 104 pitches.
This marked the first time in over two years, spanning 53 consecutive starts, that he failed to pitch at least five innings. The Phillies won the game 10-6. After being pulled following an RBI single by Nick Gonzales, Wheeler walked off the mound without acknowledging the crowd's ovation. He stated he was upset about the early removal, feeling he had earned the right to complete the inning, and had not yet spoken with manager Don Mattingly about it.
The decision stemmed from Wheeler's elevated pitch count, which reached 101 after back-to-back singles to Esmerlyn Valdez and Ryan O'Hearn with two outs. Pitching coach Caleb Cotham visited the mound, and after Wheeler allowed the soft RBI single, he was replaced by left-handed reliever Kyle Backhus, who subsequently hit two batters to force in another run. The oppressive heat, with a first-pitch temperature of 96 degrees, was also a factor. Wheeler's ERA rose from 2.03 to 2.36.
Because he did not finish the fifth inning, he was ineligible for the win, which went to a reliever. Mattingly defended the move, citing Wheeler's high pitch count and lack of early-count efficiency, while also praising his resilience. He noted that Wheeler, a two-time Cy Young Award runner-up, is sometimes underrated due to his quiet demeanor. Earlier, Mattingly had highlighted Wheeler's consistency.
The Phillies, who have a 40-19 record under Mattingly since he took over, also saw offensive contributions from Trea Turner, who hit a three-run homer in the second inning, and Alec Bohm, who added a two-run homer in the eighth. The game featured various on-field activities and post-game fireworks at Citizens Bank Park
